key_insight: A metallic alloy’s microstructure and texture can be used to infer likely alloy composition and extrusion settings, with conventional descriptors outperforming learned image and graph embeddings in this small inverse-design study.
engineering_relevance: This suggests reverse mapping from desired microstructure to manufacturing recipe could help guide alloy development and process selection when expert intuition is limited.
method: Built an in-house dataset of 107 magnesium alloy extrusion cases spanning 14 alloys, with optical micrographs and X-ray texture measurements.
Compared three structure descriptors: conventional grain/texture statistics, pretrained vision embeddings, and a graph neural network on grain networks.
Used separate prediction heads for two inverse tasks: infer composition from process conditions and infer process parameters from composition.
evidence_signal: In 5-fold cross-validation, conventional descriptors identified the correct alloy for 65% of held-out cases versus 17% for the most-common-alloy baseline, while learned embeddings stayed below 30%; microstructure roughly halved temperature error versus composition alone.
watch_item: The dataset is small and only covers a limited set of discrete alloys and press settings, so the reported inverse predictions may not generalize to broader continuous manufacturing spaces.
paper_title: Which alloy composition,what process parameters? Inferring the recipe from optimized metallic microstructure and texture
